title: Impeccable skill matching plan
purpose: Map the five vetted visual critique findings and the user-confirmed F6 story addition against every skill in the current installed 144-file universe. Select only evidence-relevant guidance; this is a read-only matching/planning artifact and does not change application source.

authority_and_scope.current_task: User-requested matching of every new, vetted critique finding to the detailed appropriate skill, source owner, visible result, and validation evidence.
preserve: Approved artwork, character identities, clothing, and current visual identity
The complete story: Hero → approved B room → InterPals first-contact chapter → Gwangju/Santo Domingo/birds/time/duel → 3D games → single letter/drawn pact → rose
All eight games, rhythm functionality, API behavior, and Korean/Spanish language support
authority_and_scope.responsive_review: The user explicitly requests the 390×844 viewport after desktop. Treat it as in scope for this task; the previous mobile-QA exclusion is superseded.
anti_goals: No generic redesign or replacement of approved identity/artwork
No effect added to conceal spatial gaps or composition problems
Do not use stale PRODUCT/DESIGN or old compact Hero/static chat assumptions as authority over current source and user approvals
Do not invent findings or reuse historical scores as new evidence
authority_and_scope.composition_gate: Before recommending visual effects, establish spatial dimensions, grouping, and the terminal B composition. A visual treatment must not obscure unresolved composition or spatial gaps.

repository_rules.relevant_excerpt: Keep the current owner; use observed evidence and corrective prompt feedback. Design backward from approved B arrival, inspect actual intermediate compositions before motion, preserve approved assets and protected functionality. Desktop evidence comes first and mobile is the final review.

Before writing, read the task and code it touches; scope callers and risks. Choose the smallest complete change. Never cut validation, error handling, security, accessibility, hardware calibration, or user-requested functionality.

impeccable.relevant_excerpt: The brief wins; refinement preserves identity. Explicit commands route to their reference. Preserve approved aesthetics and constraints; visual authority comes from evidence, not filenames.

references.name: overdrive

references.name: animate

references.name: optimize
references.matching_note: For evidenced performance bottlenecks only. Measure current state and cause first, then compare before/after without sacrificing functionality or accessibility.

references.name: live

findings.title: Early desktop Hero camera crops one partner in a held intermediate frame.

source_evidence.finding: At about 0.35 viewport-height of scroll (315px at 1440×900; normalized ScrollTrigger progress is about 0.135), editorial copy is gone, the man is clipped at the right edge and the woman is outside frame; the telescope/background remain complete. A user can stop or reverse at that state.
source_evidence.scope: Desktop captured; no 390 screenshot was vetted for this exact finding.

findings.why_primary: The defect is multi-subject camera framing in the desktop cameraKeys path: author the intermediate frustum around both partners or move the portrait out as one complete group. The skill explicitly covers group framing and cinematic blends. Apply its engine-neutral math only; do not port its Godot/Unity implementation snippets.
findings.supporting_rationale: Three.js owns the perspective camera and projection; the existing GSAP pinned timeline samples scroll progress, so forward/reverse states must remain coherent. No new animation layer is needed.
findings.expected_visible_result: At the cited stopped progress at both desktop widths, the approved couple remains framed together, or the whole portrait has exited cleanly; no isolated clipped partner is left behind. Editorial exit and B arrival retain the approved copy, faces, clothing, palette and B-room composition.

states: same normalized progress ~0.135 at reported 315px scroll for 1440×900 while scrolling forward
validation.method: Capture a forward/reverse progress sweep at the same progress values; compare the couple bounding box to the viewport edges and inspect B endpoint. Record browser/renderer; screenshots establish composition only.
validation.pass_condition: At every held intermediate frame the intended group is framed without a lone clipped partner; no direction-dependent jump; B endpoint remains the approved room.

findings.title: After the mobile rose finale, the reread link and return rows are outside the reachable document scroll extent.

source_evidence.finding: Following a real drawn signature and fold at 390px, the rose completes but normal Playwright clicks repeatedly fail because `.ec-read-again` is outside the viewport after scrolling; the last reachable frame ends at the play/ideas action row, with date, reread and footer below. Desktop reread succeeds.
source_evidence.source_evidence: closeLetter snapshots reader surface height/offset; the rose pane then uses this frozen snapshot while the finale is taller at narrow width.

findings.why_primary: Commands `adapt` + `harden`: this is a mobile-specific responsive flow failure caused by the frozen reader surface not reserving the mounted rose finale’s full scroll extent. Adapt the narrow context and harden its real completion path so the existing reread stays reachable.
findings.supporting_rationale: The engine-neutral screen-flow and navigation guidance supports reachability checks; apply it to the existing web reader and do not port game-engine UI APIs.
findings.expected_visible_result: The reader’s frozen surface reserves actual responsive rose/finale height, including top offset and return/footer rows, while preserving the in-place fold position. After the rose completes, a normal touch/pointer scroll can reach and activate the existing “read letter again” link; desktop behavior and one-letter/one-pact flow remain unchanged.

states: activate reread and confirm return to letter
validation.method: Repeat the real drawn-signature flow; record document/reader surface scrollHeight and target rect after rose mount; use normal wheel/touch scroll and a normal pointer click (no forced click or JS activation). Confirm desktop rereads still work and focus/scroll returns to reader. Emulation verifies layout/automation only, not a physical phone gesture.
validation.pass_condition: After completing signature/fold at 390×844, the reread link and footer become scroll-reachable and activate normally, no forced scroll/click; fold position remains stable; desktop reread still succeeds.

guardrails: Do not assume April 4 is the date of the first contact or assign any exact date/time.
Do not invent chat messages, timestamps, quotes, platform transcript details, or a specific first greeting.
Do not embellish the initial rudeness into a forgiveness scene or attribute emotional statements not supplied by the user.

implementation_details.gsap_outer_scroll_timeline: src/landing/FirstConversation.tsx uses GSAP 3.15 with ScrollTrigger, gsap.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)'), a scoped gsap.context, and a reversible scrub timeline. It enters the folded ribbon assembly from y=32/rotation=-2 and rotates fold groups ±4 degrees into their resting geometry.
implementation_details.motion_inner_pointer_response: The inner paper wrapper uses Motion 14 (`motion/react`): useMotionValue/useSpring/useTransform and useReducedMotion; pointer parallax clamps to ±2.4°, runs only for fine mouse hover, and resets on leave/cancel. Reduced motion disables the pointer response and outer GSAP reveal.
implementation_details.integration: post-hero-preview/src/StoryChapters.tsx renders FirstConversation immediately before the existing distance section.
